title: Renumber a BASIC program

milestone.title: From Machine Code to Modern Languages

description:
Early BASIC programs (5.02) numbered every line, and `GOTO 40` jumped to line 40. People numbered in tens to leave room for new lines, and when they ran out of room they had to **renumber**: give the lines 10, 20, 30, ... again, and fix every `GOTO` to match.

Write `renumber(program)`: `program` is a list of lines like `"40 GOTO 10"`, each starting with its number. Return the program with lines numbered 10, 20, 30, ... in the same order, and every `GOTO n` and `THEN n` changed to the line's new number.

```python
renumber(["5 PRINT \"HI\"", "7 GOTO 5"])
# ["10 PRINT \"HI\"", "20 GOTO 10"]
```

A `GOTO` to a line that does not exist stays as it was. The only places a line number appears are after `GOTO` and after `THEN`, always as a separate word.

`line.split(" ", 1)` splits off the first word; `" ".join(words)` puts words back together. A dictionary such as `new_number = {}` remembers each old number's new one: `new_number["40"] = 30`. `for i, line in enumerate(program):` gives each line with its position `i` (0, 1, 2, ...), and `str(n)` turns a number into text.
hints: Work in two passes. First, build a dictionary from each old line number to its new one (10, 20, 30 in order).
Then rewrite each line with its new number, and replace the number after every `GOTO` and `THEN` using the same dictionary.
